display.purpose: Page-level display headlines on Exam Blue surfaces. The old hero gradient-clipped keyword is retired.

title.purpose: Card titles (school names) and dialog headers.

label.purpose: Uppercase, bold, wide-tracked meta tags (type, district, eyebrows).

landing-display.purpose: Poster headline and giant tabular proof figures on the landing only. Archivo loads globally via next/font but applies only within .landing.

landing-body.purpose: The .landing base reading face. Loads globally via next/font but applies only within .landing.

landing-micro.purpose: The landing's document meta-grammar: 10-11px uppercase mono, 0.14-0.18em tracking, ink-faint — masthead tagline, axis labels, figure captions, section codes, disclaimers, errors.

admin-page-title.purpose: PageHeader h1 on every admin page; 700, tight tracking.

admin-figure.purpose: Ledger counter-strip figures; ink, missing-orange for gap counters, faint when zero.

admin-body.purpose: Body copy, controls, nav items, table cells, buttons (md).

admin-label.purpose: Form labels (600), breadcrumbs, card descriptions, small buttons.

admin-meta.purpose: Meta rows, hints, badges, table headers, sidebar group names. Sentence case; the admin has no uppercase labels.

admin-code.purpose: Only the G A T D P K M codes above the pip column (telefon is a phone icon).

blog-display.purpose: .blog only: the index "Blog" at 4 / 5.5 / 6rem, 800, line-height 0.85, at the -0.04em tracking floor.

blog-title.purpose: .blog only: article h2 (1.625 / 1.875rem) and section heads (1.375 / 1.5rem) on an ink rule, 700, -0.02em.

blog-body.purpose: .blog only: Literata with optical sizing, 1.125 / 1.1875rem, line-height 1.75, in a 68ch column.

blog-meta.purpose: .blog only: Schibsted 0.875rem, category 600 ink, tabular date and read time in muted.

blog-label.purpose: .blog only: uppercase 0.06em for the "Bu yazıda" / "Paylaş" margin labels and callout labels; never above a headline.

blog-plate-figure.purpose: .blog only: the giant key figure on a plate, container-sized (cqw/cqh) and stepped by length; 800, -0.04em.

shadows.name: resting
shadows.purpose: Default flat rest on cards, bars, inputs (both worlds).

shadows.name: card-hover-lift
shadows.purpose: School cards on hover, paired with a -2px translate.

shadows.name: action-glow
shadows.purpose: Exam Blue primary buttons; deepens to 0.4 alpha on hover. Not used on the landing (landing buttons are shadowless teal fills).

shadows.name: admin-card
shadows.purpose: .admin only: resting sheets (cards, ledger, counter strip, tab rail, docked künye panel) together with a hairline admin-line border. Scoped departure from the Exam Blue Flat-Rest Rule.

shadows.name: admin-float
shadows.purpose: .admin only: floating layers over content (bulk action bar, sticky save bar, user menu). Drawer and slide-over use the larger shadow-xl.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default easing for color/transform state transitions.

motion.name: duration-standard
motion.purpose: Hover/focus transitions on buttons, cards, inputs; also the landing axis-tick color/opacity transitions.

motion.name: landing-ease-marker
motion.purpose: Landing percentile 'sen' marker left-position slide (300ms, expo-out); first appearance uses the marker-in 300ms opacity fade.

motion.name: admin-duration-color
motion.purpose: .admin only: colour transitions on buttons, inputs, nav items, rows. No hover lifts.

motion.name: admin-duration-sidebar
motion.purpose: .admin only: sidebar width 240px <-> 72px. prefers-reduced-motion sets every transition and animation inside .admin to 0ms.

motion.name: blog-plate-in
motion.purpose: .blog only: the one motion moment; the featured plate figure unrolls from the top on the index lead and article hero. 0ms under reduced motion.

motion.name: blog-link-hover
motion.purpose: .blog only: Lemon Soft wash on link hover.

motion.name: blog-toc-marker
motion.purpose: .blog only: TOC square morphs into the 16x3 ink bar for the active section.

breakpoints.name: blog-plate-figure-tab
breakpoints.purpose: .blog only: below this plate width the figure tab on a photo plate is hidden.

adminLayout.ledgerDetailPanel: 360px docked column at xl; slide-over (max 384px) below xl
adminLayout.schoolFormTabRail: 220px sticky rail at lg; horizontal strip below lg

blogLayout.postSet: 5-col plate entry + 7-col text rows with square thumbnails (88px, 144px from sm)
blogLayout.contentsRow: 8.5rem tabular date | title + dotted leader + category | 3.5rem right-aligned tabular read time

narrative.northStar: Güvenilir Rehberlik Masası (The Trusted Guidance Desk) — with a landing-scoped sub-world: Yerleştirme Kılavuzu (The Placement Guide) — and an admin-scoped sub-world: Veri Sağlık Defteri (The Data-Health Ledger)
narrative.overview: Hedefim Lise sits with an anxious 8th-grader (and their parent, and their counselor) at the moment a life choice is being made, and its whole job is to feel like a calm, credible desk to make that choice at. The system runs on a deliberate duality: a deep-navy chrome world — the sticky navbar (#0a0f1c), the footer, and the dark page headers on interior surfaces — frames the product like a confident night sky you're navigating by, while the body is a bright, orderly workspace of near-white canvas, cool slate neutrals, and a single decisive blue. Scope note (2026-08): the landing route (/) no longer uses the old dark-navy #071426 hero with aurora glows; it runs its own light, landing-scoped document world — 'Yerleştirme Kılavuzu' — on a cool paper ground (#f3f5f4) with petrol teal (#0c4a45) as authority/action and vermilion (#dc5a34) as the single warm signal for the user's own position, set in Archivo + Source Serif 4 + mono micro-labels. Everything else stays Exam Blue. Admin scope (2026-09): every /admin route runs its own .admin-scoped world, "Veri Sağlık Defteri" — a data-health ledger, not a KPI dashboard. A cool violet-grey ground (#f4f5fa), white sheets and a white grouped sidebar, ledger ink (#1e2235), one indigo (#4f46e5) reserved for wayfinding, emerald/amber/rose/orange only as meaning. Inter on a fixed rem scale with tabular figures; eight fixed health pips per school (filled / outlined / dash) are the signature.
keyCharacteristics: Dark, trustworthy chrome (navbar, footer, interior page headers) over a bright, scannable data body.
One decisive accent (Exam Blue) rationed against a broad cool-slate neutral field.
Soft, resting surfaces — generous radii, hairline borders, whisper-light shadows.
Semantic color (emerald/rose/amber) used only to carry meaning, never decoration.
Calm density: roomy on marketing surfaces, efficient but never cramped in tools.
Landing-scoped document world (.landing only): paper ground, teal authority, one vermilion 'sen' signal, poster-scale tabular figures, mono micro-label meta-grammar.
Admin-scoped ledger world (.admin only): grey ground, white sheets, indigo for wayfinding only, eight fixed shape-coded health pips per school, fixed rem type, sentence case, tabular figures.

rules.name: The One-Signal Rule
rules.body: Exam Blue is the only color that invites action. It should cover well under ~10% of any body screen — its scarcity is what makes 'act here' legible. Never use blue as a decorative fill.

rules.name: The Meaning-Only Rule
rules.body: Emerald, rose, and amber never appear for decoration — each is a claim (good / destructive / caution). If a color isn't carrying meaning, it's slate.

rules.name: The Two-Worlds Rule (amended 2026-08)
rules.body: Cyan and glow treatments live only in the dark chrome world (navbar, footer, dark interior page headers). The light Exam Blue body is blue-and-slate. The old third member — the dark aurora hero — no longer exists: the landing is now its own light document world, and neither cyan, aurora glows, nor Exam Blue may appear inside it.

rules.name: The Heavy-Head Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is carried by weight, not size alone: headings are 700–800 with slightly negative tracking; body stays 400–500. Never set a heading below 700.

rules.name: The Uppercase-Label Rule
rules.body: Category/meta text is uppercase, bold, wide-tracked, and tiny (≤11px). It is a texture, not a headline — never uppercase running copy.

rules.name: The Flat-Rest Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest and defined by their hairline border. Shadow is a response to state (hover, focus) — never ambient decoration on a static card.

rules.name: The Sen Rule (landing)
rules.body: Vermilion marks exactly one thing: you. It never fills a button, tints a card, or decorates. If vermilion appears, it is either the user's position on the scale or an error the user must act on.

rules.name: The One-Authority Rule (landing)
rules.body: Teal is the only action color on the landing. Exam Blue never crosses into .landing; teal/vermilion never leave it.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule (landing)
rules.body: Every numeral that represents data gets font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums (the .tabular utility).

rules.name: The Turkish-Comma Rule (landing)
rules.body: Every percentile prints with a comma decimal (5,00, %1,23) via the shared fmt() pattern. Never a dot.

rules.name: The Sort-Not-Filter Rule (landing)
rules.body: The percentile input is a sort signal, never a threshold filter: submit routes to /okullar sorted by percentile. No school is ever hidden by the user's number.

rules.name: The Wayfinding Rule (admin)
rules.body: Indigo means "you are here" or "go here", and nothing else: active nav, selected row, the one filled primary per screen, the focus ring, the unread badge, and links. It never colours a status, a figure, a success icon, or a decorative fill. State belongs to emerald, amber, rose and missing-orange.

rules.name: The Meaning-Only Rule (admin)
rules.body: Emerald, amber, rose and orange appear only as claims: ok / passive or unsaved / destructive or error / missing. A counter with nothing to report drops to admin-faint, not to a colour.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule (admin)
rules.body: Every figure that is compared or counted carries tabular numerals: counters, nav counts, "N okul seçildi", "N / N tamam", table dates.

rules.name: The Sentence-Case Rule (admin)
rules.body: Every label, group name, button and header is sentence case in Turkish ("Toplu yükleme", "Yeni okul", "Okunmamış mesaj"). The admin has no uppercase, no wide tracking, and no eyebrow labels; the Exam Blue Uppercase-Label Rule does not apply inside .admin.

rules.name: The Never-Colour-Only Rule (admin)
rules.body: State is carried by shape first: ok = a filled emerald square, missing = an outlined orange square (1.5px border on white), not required = a dash in line-strong. Each pip has a title ("Görsel: eksik"), and the row carries a screen-reader sentence ("Eksik: Görsel, Telefon" or "Eksik yok").

rules.name: The Fixed-Row Rule (admin)
rules.body: Eight pips, always in the same order and position, 4px apart, never wrapping (whitespace-nowrap), so columns can be scanned down the ledger. Size is 10px in rows and 12px in the panel.

rules.name: The One-Vocabulary Rule (admin)
rules.body: The whole admin uses the same three words for data state: tamam / eksik / gerekmez, and the same pair for publish state: Yayında / Pasif. The legend above the ledger defines both the states and the eight codes (codes only at md and up, where the code header is visible).

rules.name: The Newest-Post Rule (blog)
rules.body: Lemon is never a category tone. Categories take ink or paper only (plateTone() in src/lib/blog.ts: fixed for known categories, hashed across ink/paper for new ones). The lemon plate belongs to exactly one post, the blog's newest (all[0]), and it stays lemon on the index, on its own page and in every related list, so readers learn to spot it.

rules.name: The Fill-Not-Text Rule (blog)
rules.body: Lemon appears as a flood, a stroke or a marker. On white it never carries words; on ink it may carry the plate figure or an icon.

rules.name: The Tracking-Floor Rule (blog)
rules.body: No blog type is tracked tighter than -0.04em; only the monumental title and plate figures reach it.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule (blog)
rules.body: Every date, count, read time, page number, ordered-list number and table cell is tabular, so columns align down the contents page.

rules.name: The One-Monument Rule (blog)
rules.body: One face does the monumental work: the grotesk. Literata never sets a head or a figure.

dos: Do ration Exam Blue (#2563eb) to the single most important action per surface; keep it well under ~10% of a body screen.
Do define surfaces with hairline Line (#e2e8f0) borders and keep them flat at rest; let shadow appear only on hover/focus.
Do use the uppercase, bold, wide-tracked ≤11px label for category/meta text, and carry hierarchy with weight (700–800 heads).
Do keep radii in the 12 / 16–24px family and never mix radii within one component.
Do reserve emerald/rose/amber for genuine meaning (success / destructive / caution).
Do confine cyan and glow treatments to the dark chrome world (navbar, footer, dark interior page headers) only.
Do carry all landing meta text in the mono micro-label voice (10–11px, uppercase, 0.14–0.18em tracking, ink-faint).
Do keep landing panels flat: Line hairline + shadow-sm, hover states only.
Do keep every admin value on the admin-* utilities; new admin surfaces compose AdminPage, PageHeader, Card, AdminButton and the adminControl/adminLabel/adminHint strings rather than restyling.
Do give each screen exactly one filled indigo primary; all other actions are secondary, ghost, or danger.

Do make destructive actions quiet: danger-variant text or icon buttons (never a filled red button) behind a confirmation (ConfirmButton or a window.confirm on submit) that names the record and the consequence.
Do carry state with shape plus text (filled / outlined / dash, dot + word) and the one state vocabulary.
Do set counted figures in tabular numerals, and keep labels in sentence case.
Do keep every blog value on the blog-* utilities and compose BlogFrame, Plate, PostMeta, PostSet and ContentsRow rather than restyling.
Do give each plate one flood colour, and give lemon only to the newest post's plate and the empty state; categories get ink or paper.
Do put a post's key figure in highlight so its plate carries a number, not just a category name.
Do mark state by shape (square → bar, fill → tab) and keep figures tabular.
Do separate sections with the 2px ink rule and rows with Line hairlines.
donts: Don't mix gray-* and slate-* neutrals; the system is slate — legacy gray-* classes (mobile sheets) are drift to migrate.
Don't introduce a second accent hue into the Exam Blue body; blue is the only action color there.
Don't put gradient-clipped text or cyan glows on body/data surfaces — they belong to the dark chrome world, and the old hero devices (aurora, gradient keyword) are retired entirely.
Don't cross the landing boundary in either direction: no Exam Blue/cyan inside .landing, no landing teal/vermilion/Archivo/Source Serif on Exam Blue surfaces.
Don't add ambient drop-shadows to resting cards; depth is tonal + hairline first.
Don't set headings below 700 weight or uppercase running body copy.
Don't use vermilion for anything but the user's position or an actionable error on the landing.
Don't turn the landing percentile input into a filter, print a percentile with a dot decimal, or set data numerals without .tabular.
Don't use indigo for status, success, figures or decoration; don't use emerald, amber, rose or orange without a meaning.
Don't add KPI cards or charts that don't filter the ledger; counters are links.
Don't add uppercase eyebrows, wide-tracked labels, fluid display type, or hover lifts inside .admin.
Don't reorder, wrap or drop pips, or signal a pip state by colour alone.
Don't let Exam Blue, cyan, landing teal/vermilion, or the landing fonts into .admin.
Don't lay out recent or related posts as an equal three-up card grid; use the unequal 5 + 7 set.
Don't put a running head, eyebrow or kicker on a plate or above a headline.
Don't set text in lemon on white, or use lemon as a category tone.
Don't add shadows, gradients (other than the highlighter band and ruled texture), or radii above 4px inside .blog.
Don't let Exam Blue, cyan, landing teal/vermilion, admin indigo, or another world's fonts into .blog.
